The user wants assembly code (AVR assembler) for Arduino Mega to sample INA219 as fast as possible in 12-bit, 128-average mode. Let me think about this.

INA219 is an I2C current/power monitor. 12-bit ADC, averaging 128 samples. The conversion time for 12-bit is 532µs per sample, times 128 averages = ~68ms plus overhead. So the I2C transaction wait dominates.

They want "fastest sampling" — the optimal approach is to keep the INA219 in continuous conversion mode and just read the last result register as fast as I2C allows, rather than triggering single-shot conversions.

- Bits 10-7: Bus ADC resolution/averaging
- Bits 6-3: Shunt ADC resolution/averaging
- Bits 2-0: Mode (111 = shunt and bus continuous)

For 12-bit, 128 samples averaging: the ADC setting code is 0b1111 = 0xF. Let me check the table:

At 16MHz, 400kHz: TWBR = ((F_CPU/SCL) - 16) / 2 = ((16000000/400000)-16)/2 = (40-16)/2 = 12. Prescaler 1.

Key point about "fastest sampling": Set the config once with continuous mode + 128 averaging. Then loop reading the shunt voltage register (0x01) as fast as I2C allows. But the underlying conversion updates only every ~68ms. So polling faster than the conversion rate just returns duplicate data. If they want distinct samples at the device's max rate, they must either use continuous mode and read at 68ms intervals (checking the CNVR bit), or trigger single conversions.

Actually "fastest sampling in 12-bit 128-average mode" is inherently limited by 68ms. The fastest way to get every new sample is: continuous mode, and read whenever conversion ready. To guarantee you don't miss any and read as soon as ready, you can poll the conversion-ready flag. In continuous mode, the CNVR bit (bit 1 of bus voltage register 0x02) toggles after each conversion.

Alternatively single-shot triggered reads: write config with mode=001 (shunt single) then poll, then read. That's slower due to repeated register writes.

Best is continuous + read bus voltage register (which contains CNVR flag) to detect new data, then read shunt/current.

.equ INA_ADDR_W, (INA_ADDR<<1)|0     ; 0x80

.equ INA_SHUNT,  0x01
.equ INA_BUS,    0x02
.equ INA_POWER,  0x03
.equ INA_CURRENT,0x04
.equ INA_CALIB,  0x05

.equ TWI_TWBR, 0xB8
...
```

;******************************************************************************
; ina219_fast.S  --  INA219 fastest sampling, 12-bit / 128-sample averaging
;
; Target : Arduino Mega 2560 / ATmega2560, 16 MHz, TWI @ 400 kHz
; Tool   : avr-gcc (GNU as) - just drop this file in your sketch folder.
;
; INA219 wiring (Mega):
;   VCC  -> 3.3V or 5V (module has LDO)   GND -> GND
;   SDA  -> D20 (PD1)                     SCL -> D21 (PD0)
;   External 4.7k..10k pull-ups to VCC on SDA/SCL are required for 400 kHz.
;
; Device timing fact:
;   12-bit + 128 averages => ~68.1 ms per conversion (datasheet).  That is the
;   hard ceiling: you can get at most ~14.7 fresh samples per second.
;   The code below therefore (a) leaves the INA219 free-running in continuous
;   mode and (b) polls the Conversion-Ready flag so each fresh sample is
;   captured with the smallest possible latency.
;******************************************************************************

#include <avr/io.h>

;---- INA219 -----------------------------------------------------------------
.equ INA_ADDR,  0x40              ; A1=A0=GND  (0x40) ; 0x41/0x44/0x45 possible
.equ INA_ADDR_W, (INA_ADDR<<1)          ; 0x80  SLA+W
.equ INA_ADDR_R, (INA_ADDR<<1)|1        ; 0x81  SLA+R

.equ REG_CONFIG,  0x00
.equ REG_SHUNT,   0x01
.equ REG_BUS,     0x02
.equ REG_POWER,   0x03
.equ REG_CURRENT, 0x04
.equ REG_CAL,     0x05

; Configuration word 0x3FFF:
;   bit15   RST  = 0
;   bit14:13 BRNG= 01  -> 32 V bus range
;   bit12:11 PGA = 11  -> +-320 mV shunt range
;   bit10:7  BADC= 1111-> bus ADC  12-bit, 128 samples
;   bit6:3   SADC= 1111-> shunt ADC 12-bit, 128 samples
;   bit2:0   MODE= 111 -> shunt+bus continuous
.equ INA_CONFIG, 0x3FFF

; Calibration register.  cal = trunc( 0.04096 / (current_LSB * Rshunt) )
; Example: Rshunt = 0.1 ohm, current_LSB = 100 uA  ->  cal = 4096
.equ INA_CAL,    4096

; TWI: SCL = F_CPU / (16 + 2*TWBR*4^TWPS) = 16e6/(16+2*12) = 400 kHz
.equ TWI_TWBR_400K, 12

;******************************************************************************
; ina219_fast.S  -  fastest INA219 sampling, 12-bit ADC + 128-sample averaging
;
; Target : Arduino Mega 2560 / ATmega2560 @ 16 MHz, TWI (I2C) @ 400 kHz
; Tool   : avr-gcc / GNU as.  Drop this file in your sketch folder; the Arduino
;          builder assembles *.S with the C preprocessor automatically.
;
; Wiring (Mega 2560):
;     INA219 VCC -> 3V3 or 5V (breakout has an LDO)      GND -> GND
;     INA219 SDA -> D20 (PD1)                            SCL -> D21 (PD0)
;     Use external 4.7k..10k pull-ups to VCC on SDA/SCL for 400 kHz.
;
; Why this is the fastest possible:
;   12-bit + 128 averages = one conversion every ~68.1 ms (datasheet), i.e. a
;   hard ceiling of ~14.7 fresh samples per second - the I2C bus is *not* the
;   bottleneck.  So we let the INA219 free-run in continuous mode and poll the
;   Conversion-READY flag (CNVR) so every fresh sample is grabbed with the
;   smallest possible latency (~one register read after it becomes ready).
;
;   Data-sheet note used here: CNVR (bus-voltage register, bit 1) is cleared by
;   writing a new mode into the config register OR by *reading the Power
;   register*.  Reading the bus-voltage register does NOT clear it.  Therefore:
;       poll bus-voltage reg for CNVR == 1  ->  read Power (clears CNVR)
;       ->  read Shunt, Current.
;******************************************************************************

#include <avr/io.h>              ; symbolic SFR names (resolved as MEM addresses)

;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
; INA219
;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
.equ INA_ADDR,   0x40                       ; A1=A0=GND -> 0x40
.equ INA_ADDR_W, (INA_ADDR << 1)            ; 0x80  SLA+W
.equ INA_ADDR_R, (INA_ADDR << 1) | 1        ; 0x81  SLA+R

.equ REG_CONFIG,  0x00
.equ REG_SHUNT,   0x01
.equ REG_BUS,     0x02
.equ REG_POWER,   0x03
.equ REG_CURRENT, 0x04
.equ REG_CAL,     0x05

; Configuration word = 0x3FFF  ->
;   bit15    RST   = 0
;   bit14:13 BRNG  = 01   -> bus voltage range 32 V
;   bit12:11 PGA   = 11   -> shunt range +/-320 mV
;   bit10:7  BADC  = 1111 -> bus   ADC  12-bit, 128 samples
;   bit6:3   SADC  = 1111 -> shunt ADC  12-bit, 128 samples
;   bit2:0   MODE  = 111  -> shunt + bus, continuous
; (change bit10:7 / bit6:3 for other averaging, see datasheet table)
.equ INA_CONFIG, 0x3FFF

; Calibration:  cal = trunc( 0.04096 / (current_LSB * Rshunt) )
;   Rshunt = 0.1 ohm, current_LSB = 100 uA  ->  cal = 4096
.equ INA_CAL,    4096

;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
; TWI bit-rate divisor.  SCL = F_CPU / (16 + 2*TWBR*4^TWPS),  TWPS = 0
;   400 kHz -> TWBR = 12 ;   100 kHz -> TWBR = 72
;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
.equ TWI_TWBR,   12

;=============================================================================
;  RAM visible to the C / .ino side
;=============================================================================
.section .bss
.global ina_shunt
ina_shunt:   .space 2          ; latest raw shunt voltage   (signed, 10 uV/LSB)
.global ina_bus
ina_bus:     .space 2          ; latest raw bus voltage      (bit15..3 = 4mV/LSB)
.global ina_current
ina_current: .space 2          ; latest raw current          (signed)
.global ina_power
ina_power:   .space 2          ; latest raw power
.global ina_head
ina_head:    .space 1          ; ring buffer write index (wraps 0..255)
.global ina_count
ina_count:   .space 4          ; 32-bit count of captured samples
.global ina_buf
ina_buf:     .space 512        ; 256 x uint16_t ring buffer of raw shunt data

.section .text

;=============================================================================
;  TWI primitives.
;  NOTE: on the ATmega2560 the TWI registers are in extended I/O (>= 0x40),
;  so they can only be reached with lds/sts - in/out cannot encode them.
;=============================================================================

;--- wait for the current TWI op to finish ; return masked status in r24 ------
twi_wait:
    lds  r24, TWCR
    sbrs r24, TWINT
    rjmp twi_wait
    lds  r24, TWSR
    andi r24, 0xF8              ; drop prescaler bits
    ret

;--- START / repeated START --------------------------------------------------
twi_start:
    ldi  r24, (1<<TWINT)|(1<<TWSTA)|(1<<TWEN)
    sts  TWCR, r24
    rjmp twi_wait

;--- STOP (waits until the bus is actually released) -------------------------
twi_stop:
    ldi  r19, (1<<TWINT)|(1<<TWSTO)|(1<<TWEN)
    sts  TWCR, r19
1:  lds  r19, TWCR
    sbrc r19, TWSTO
    rjmp 1b
    ret

;--- send byte in r24 --------------------------------------------------------
twi_write:
    sts  TWDR, r24
    ldi  r24, (1<<TWINT)|(1<<TWEN)
    sts  TWCR, r24
    rjmp twi_wait

;--- receive byte, ACK, -> r24 ----------------------------------------------
twi_read_ack:
    ldi  r24, (1<<TWINT)|(1<<TWEN)|(1<<TWEA)
    sts  TWCR, r24
1:  lds  r24, TWCR
    sbrs r24, TWINT
    rjmp 1b
    lds  r24, TWDR
    ret

;--- receive last byte, NACK, -> r24 ----------------------------------------
twi_read_nack:
    ldi  r24, (1<<TWINT)|(1<<TWEN)
    sts  TWCR, r24
1:  lds  r24, TWCR
    sbrs r24, TWINT
    rjmp 1b
    lds  r24, TWDR
    ret

;=============================================================================
;  INA219 register access
;=============================================================================

;--- write 16-bit reg:  in  r24 = reg, r23:r22 = value (r23 = MSB) -----------
ina_write_reg:
    mov  r19, r24               ; save reg pointer
    mov  r20, r23               ; save MSB
    mov  r21, r22               ; save LSB
    rcall twi_start
    ldi  r24, INA_ADDR_W
    rcall twi_write
    mov  r24, r19
    rcall twi_write
    mov  r24, r20
    rcall twi_write
    mov  r24, r21
    rcall twi_write
    rcall twi_stop
    ret

;--- read 16-bit reg:  in  r24 = reg  ->  out r25:r24 = value (r25 = MSB) -----
ina_read_reg:
    mov  r18, r24               ; save reg pointer
    rcall twi_start             ; START
    ldi  r24, INA_ADDR_W
    rcall twi_write
    mov  r24, r18
    rcall twi_write
    rcall twi_start             ; repeated START
    ldi  r24, INA_ADDR_R
    rcall twi_write
    rcall twi_read_ack          ; MSB (master ACKs)
    mov  r25, r24
    rcall twi_read_nack         ; LSB (master NACKs)
    rcall twi_stop
    ret

;=============================================================================
;  Public API
;=============================================================================

;--- void ina219_init(void) --------------------------------------------------
.global ina219_init
ina219_init:
    ; --- TWI master, 400 kHz ---
    ldi  r24, TWI_TWBR
    sts  TWBR, r24
    ldi  r24, 0x00
    sts  TWSR, r24              ; prescaler = 1
    sts  TWAR, r24              ; own address (unused in master mode)
    ldi  r24, (1<<TWEN)
    sts  TWCR, r24              ; enable TWI

    ; --- INA219: 12-bit, x128 averaging, continuous ---
    ldi  r24, REG_CONFIG
    ldi  r22, lo8(INA_CONFIG)
    ldi  r23, hi8(INA_CONFIG)
    rcall ina_write_reg

    ; --- INA219: calibration ---
    ldi  r24, REG_CAL
    ldi  r22, lo8(INA_CAL)
    ldi  r23, hi8(INA_CAL)
    rcall ina_write_reg

    ret

;--- void ina219_sample(void) --
;    Blocks until the INA219 reports a fresh conversion (CNVR), then latches
;    bus / power / shunt / current into the ina_* globals, appends the raw
;    shunt value to the ina_buf ring buffer and bumps ina_count.
.global ina219_sample
ina219_sample:
poll:
    ldi  r24, REG_BUS
    rcall ina_read_reg
    sbrs r24, 1                 ; CNVR set ?
    rjmp poll                   ; not ready -> keep polling

    sts  ina_bus,   r24         ; bus voltage (top 13 bits + CNVR/OVF)
    sts  ina_bus+1, r25

    ldi  r24, REG_POWER         ; reading Power clears CNVR
    rcall ina_read_reg
    sts  ina_power,   r24
    sts  ina_power+1, r25

    ldi  r24, REG_SHUNT
    rcall ina_read_reg
    sts  ina_shunt,   r24
    sts  ina_shunt+1, r25
    ; ---- append r25:r24 to the ring buffer ----
    ldi  r30, lo8(ina_buf)
    ldi  r31, hi8(ina_buf)
    lds  r18, ina_head
    mov  r19, r18
    lsl  r19                    ; index * 2
    add  r30, r19
    brcc 1f
    inc  r31
1:  st   Z,   r24
    std  Z+1, r25
    inc  r18
    sts  ina_head, r18

    ldi  r24, REG_CURRENT
    rcall ina_read_reg
    sts  ina_current,   r24
    sts  ina_current+1, r25

    ; ---- ina_count++ (32-bit) ----
    lds  r18, ina_count
    lds  r19, ina_count+1
    lds  r20, ina_count+2
    lds  r21, ina_count+3
    subi r18, 0xFF
    sbci r19, 0xFF
    sbci r20, 0xFF
    sbci r21, 0xFF
    sts  ina_count,   r18
    sts  ina_count+1, r19
    sts  ina_count+2, r20
    sts  ina_count+3, r21
    ret

;--- void ina219_run(void) -- never returns; free-running sampler -------------
.global ina219_run
ina219_run:
    rcall ina219_sample
    rjmp  ina219_run

;=============================================================================
;  Alternative: if you only want the absolute maximum *register read* rate
;  (ignoring sample freshness), replace ina219_sample's poll with a plain
;  tight loop that reads REG_SHUNT over and over - the INA219 just returns its
;  last completed conversion each time.  Storage would then itself filter
;  duplicates.  Not shown here because it stores many copies of each sample.
;=============================================================================

### Key design point
At 12-bit + 128 averages the INA219 produces one conversion every **~68.1 ms** — so I²C is *not* the bottleneck.     ldi  r31, hi8(ina_buf)
    lds  r18, ina_head
    mov  r19, r18
    lsl  r19                    ; index * 2
    add  r30, r19
    brcc 1f
    inc  r31
1:  st   Z,   r24
    std  Z+1, r25
    inc  r18
    sts  ina_head, r18

    ldi  r24, REG_CURRENT
    rcall ina_read_reg
    sts  ina_current,   r24
    sts  ina_current+1, r25

    ; ---- ina_count++ (32-bit) ----
    lds  r18, ina_count
    lds  r19, ina_count+1
    lds  r20, ina_count+2
    lds  r21, ina_count+3
    subi r18, 0xFF
    sbci r19, 0xFF
    sbci r20, 0xFF
    sbci r21, 0xFF
    sts  ina_count,   r18
    sts  ina_count+1, r19
    sts  ina_count+2, r20
    sts  ina_count+3, r21
    ret

;--- void ina219_run(void) -- never returns; free-running sampler -------------
.global ina219_run
ina219_run:
    rcall ina219_sample
    rjmp  ina219_run
```

### How it works / speed
- **Throughput**: bounded by the device — 1 sample / 68.1 ms ≈ **14.7 Hz**.
- **Latency**: each bus-voltage poll is one 2-byte read ≈ 100 µs at 400 kHz, so a ready sample is captured < ~120 µs after it lands.
- **One-shot vs continuous**: continuous mode avoids a config write + conversion-wait per sample, so it's the fastest fresh-sample rate.
- **Accuracy of detection**: `sbrs r24, 1` tests CNVR (bit 1); the Power read then clears it so the next conversion is detected as an edge.

### Tweaks
- **Other averages** (datasheet table, config bits 10:7 / 6:3): `0011`=12-bit/1, `1001`=2, `1010`=4, `1011`=8, `1100`=16, `1101`=32, `1110`=64, `1111`=128.
- **16 V bus range / ±40 mV PGA**: change `INA_CONFIG` accordingly.
- **I²C address**: change `INA_ADDR` (0x40/0x41/0x44/0x45).
- **Slower bus** if wiring is marginal: `TWI_TWBR = 72` (100 kHz).
- **Calibration**: `INA_CAL` follows `trunc(0.04096 / (current_LSB · R_shunt))`.

### Using it
Put both files in one sketch folder. From `ina219_fast_demo.ino`:

```cpp
void setup() { Serial.begin(115200); ina219_init(); }
void loop() {
  ina219_sample();                    // ~68 ms blocking, one fresh sample
  int16_t sh = (int16_t)ina_shunt;    // 10 µV/LSB
  // ... print/scale as needed
}
```

`ina219_run()` is also exported if you want the MCU to spend all its time sampling (e.g. you inspect the `ina_buf` ring buffer and `ina_count` later, or feed an ISR).

One caveat worth knowing: if you instead want the *maximum raw register-read rate* ignoring freshness, replace the CNVR poll with a tight loop reading `REG_SHUNT` — you'll get ~8 kHz of reads, but most are duplicates of the same 68 ms-old conversion. The version above is the fastest way to get *distinct* samples.
